instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Use the Right Vocabulary
cards.instruction: Perform belonging by using official language confidently, adjusting each term whenever someone reveals what it actually means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First day in accounts and I've reconciled the invoice: right drawer. That filing system I taught you still serves us well.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's filing. Reconciliation means matching it to our records.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're finally using precise labels. Filed, then. I'll reconcile it against this quote.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's an estimate. You need the purchase order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An estimate, of course. Bring me the purchase order. You're labelling things as clearly as I used to make you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My first club meeting, and I second the minutes. You read them clearly; those speaking lessons I gave you paid off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You second a motion. I'm proposing we approve the minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A motion, yes. I second yours unanimously. You used to need me to prompt a whole sentence; look at you now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Unanimous means everyone agrees. Ruth hasn't voted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unanimity pending Ruth, then. Ask her for her vote, loudly; I taught you to reach the back row, and she's sitting in it.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: More Official Than You
cards.instruction: Turn every suggestion into a contest over whose method, title, precedent, or paperwork is more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your picnic rota is a useful draft. Mine has committee approval. I taught you to put the authorising body at the top, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine got everyone to bring sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've finally filled the food column. Mine establishes who was entitled to request those sandwiches. You skipped the heading again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then approve mine. We've already started eating.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll attach it as an appendix to mine. Put 'supporting rota' where I showed you; your sandwiches can come under my committee approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your proposed wave is cheerful. I taught you the ceremonial bow; mine follows the founder's original diagram, not a guess at friendliness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The founder asked us to wave instead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: His diagram is in the constitution. You used to forget to check the document before following a voice from the front row.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's signed my programme: 'Please wave'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Well done, you finally got something in writing. Mark it 'personal exception', as I showed you. I'll bow for everyone still governed by the constitution.

cards.title: A Valuable Safeguard
cards.instruction: Treat every delay, restriction, and extra step as evidence that the system is becoming safer and more thorough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've added a fourth inspection to our climbing wall. Wonderful. You finally asked for all the checks I taught you before opening the gates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Opening's delayed another month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A month without an uninspected climb. Put it on the calendar; you used to rush straight from checking a rope to inviting people up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll lose the whole season.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the members it's our safest season: not one uninspected climb. You've finally stopped rushing people up the wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two signatures on every trip consent form now. Reassuring. I taught you not to trust your first check; here's another pair of eyes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the only teacher here. We'll have to wait for June.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're finally waiting instead of checking your own work twice. No child boards until she's seen the forms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: June wrote them. She wants someone else to check her work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better, she's learnt the same lesson. Find a third checker, and ask who checks them; you can make that extra safeguard part of the trip plan.

cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Warmly Enforced
cards.instruction: Remain kind and welcoming while enforcing increasingly restrictive rules without exception.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm so glad you're staying. The guest bed's yours; no food upstairs. I remember teaching you to carry a plate without leaving crumbs all the way to bed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll eat breakfast downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely, you remembered that part. After nine, please; we keep the kitchen quiet before then. I'll set your place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train's at eight. Can I take a banana?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd love you to have breakfast with us. Food stays in the kitchen, though. Shall I help you find a later train?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to the swimming club! I taught you your first strokes; look how far you've come. You're very welcome to watch until your induction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I join today's induction?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once you've observed one, certainly. You finally ask before jumping in! Today you can watch from the gallery; I'll show you the stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The gallery's closed. Can I watch from poolside?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd love to bring you down, but poolside needs induction. Let's sit with a brochure; I can point out the lane where I taught you to float.

cards.title: There Is a Process
cards.instruction: Treat every favor, feeling, and urgent need as a request requiring terms, documentation, review, and approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I reassure you about the wedding, say exactly what I'm guaranteeing. I taught you to ask for something specific, not just look frightened at me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That it'll be okay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put it into words; that's progress. Weather, marriage or catering? Tick one so I can send it for the right approval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just need a hug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Much more specific. I'll amend the request: one-time comfort or reassurance throughout the ceremony? Put the duration in before I approve it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend you my umbrella once we approve the loan. I taught you to say when something comes back; what's the proposed return date?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: When this rain stops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remembered a condition this time. It's open-ended, though. Name a guarantor who'll return it if you're delayed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm getting soaked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll hold the umbrella over the form. Write 'urgent' at the top, then sign; you used to blur the terms before I'd finished checking them.
